source:
a Casual Strategy / Auto-Battler
The Elevator Pitch: Build custom miniature armies on dioramas (like tabletop battlefields) and pit them against other players in fast-paced 3-minute tactical battles.
Core Gameplay:
Collect, level up, and customize mini-figurines (Knights, Mages, Mech-Warriors).
Position units on a grid before the match starts; once battle begins, units automatically fight based on their programmed behaviors and synergies.
Unlock board themes (volcano tabletop, desktop cluttered with books, floating island diorama).
Why It Works: Strategy games on Roblox are growing rapidly, and collectible unit mechanics provide strong retention loops.

answers.ask: Is the board built at true miniature scale with the players as giants looking down, or avatar-scale ground the camera pulls back from?
answers.answer: Use true miniature-scale dioramas, with players viewing and placing their figurines from an overhead tabletop perspective.

answers.ask: How many squares across is the grid?
answers.answer: Use a compact 6-by-6 grid to keep pre-battle placement quick and readable for three-minute matches.

answers.ask: Do the three board themes need to exist at once, or is one loaded per match?
answers.answer: Load one board theme per match; volcano tabletop, cluttered desktop, and floating-island diorama are unlocked selectable themes.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: Is the board built at true miniature scale with the players as giants looking down, or avatar-scale ground the camera pulls back from? A: Use true miniature-scale dioramas, with players viewing and placing their figurines from an overhead tabletop perspective.
- [author] shape — Q: How many squares across is the grid? A: Use a compact 6-by-6 grid to keep pre-battle placement quick and readable for three-minute matches.
- [author] goal — Q: Do the three board themes need to exist at once, or is one loaded per match? A: Load one board theme per match; volcano tabletop, cluttered desktop, and floating-island diorama are unlocked selectable themes.

## Enriched image prompt
Create three separately loaded true-miniature-scale auto-battler dioramas viewed from an overhead tabletop perspective. Every variant uses the same compact 6-by-6 square placement grid with clearly readable cells and opposing deployment sides for small knight, mage, and mech-warrior figurines. Dress one board as a volcanic tabletop with dark rock and glowing lava around the playable grid; one as a desktop board framed by oversized books and desk clutter; and one as a floating-island diorama with the gridded battlefield contained on a single suspended landmass. Only one complete themed board appears in a match at a time, and set dressing must not obscure or deform any of the 36 playable cells.

## Genre
The genre is Strategy. The author's self-declared casual auto-battler is a grid-based tactical board game; collecting and leveling figurines are mechanics rather than additional layout genres.

## Shape and preset
Use `board-grid`, Zone (Board Grid), for the true-miniature 6-by-6 board that players act on without walking through. Match the Board & Card Games preset.

## Config requirements
Use `tile-grid` for exactly 36 evenly divided square cells arranged 6 by 6. Preserve visible opposing deployment halves and keep every cell unobstructed. The volcano rock and lava, oversized books and desktop clutter, and single floating island are three scene-specific dressing variants rather than extra gameplay options.

## Layout requirements
Place 36 free-text BuildZones, one centered on each grid cell, to receive pre-battle figurines. Divide them into two opposing sets of 18 cells, one deployment half per opponent, while retaining the same cell coordinates across all three board variants. No player traversal spawns are needed.

## Layout components
Build three map segments, each with shape `board-grid` and kind map: Volcano Tabletop, Cluttered Desktop, and Floating-Island Diorama. Each segment contains one 6-by-6 miniature grid, two opposite 18-cell deployment halves, and perimeter dressing kept outside the playable cells. The volcanic map uses dark rock and visible lava around the grid; the desktop map uses books and desk clutter as oversized framing props; the floating-island map uses one suspended island carrying the whole board. Compose each variant from overhead so all 36 cells and miniature figurines remain readable.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: exact cell count and alignment must lead, while `authored_plan` is not supported for a board grid.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use small scale, corresponding to Room, because miniature grid cells and figurines are the smallest required details. The themes are volcanic tabletop, cluttered desktop, and floating-island diorama. Use `P4` because the three selectable boards are separate maps loaded one per match, plus `SET` because nobody walks on the miniature boards.
